title: A Pawn Down and Holding
setup: White's king on b5 wants the sixth rank, and from there it walks your king away from the pawn's path. Black to move, and it is a draw.
hint: White's king needs a6, b6 or c6. A rook standing on a rank covers every square of it.
explanation:
## The Idea

Ranks are counted from White's side here. White's king needs a6, b6 or c6 to come up beside its pawn, and one rook move takes all three: {{Re6}}. A rook on a rank is a fence, and a king may not step onto a square it covers.

Every other move lets the king onto the sixth, in front of its own pawn, where no check from behind can reach it, and the pawn walks in.
